title: Common Evidence Definitions (v2.8)
description: Shared definitions for Business Wallet evidence objects. hash_mode selects raw-byte hashing (the default) or the optional JSON-canonicalisation modes (jcs-sha256/jcs-sha512); the alg/hash_mode/hex triple is constrained to be internally coherent (SHA-256 => 64 hex, SHA-512 => 128 hex); the Uid pattern uses the canonical hyphen separator.

Uid.description: Canonical UID form: EU-CC-SCHEME-PAYLOAD(12)C1C2, where C1 C2 are two Crockford Base32 Reed-Solomon check symbols over GF(2^5) (umbrella §3.3 / Annex F). Hyphen is the only valid separator; canonical form is upper-case.

BwAddress.description: Canonical bw: address (umbrella Annex A): bw:uid:<UID> (entity), .../u/<MID> (member), or .../r/<role> (role). The role token is RoleName (case-sensitive, lowercase); the MID token is a well-formed MID. Addresses are compared byte-exact after normalisation; percent-encoding is not permitted.

RoleName.description: A role token (X-16): the SAME grammar used in a bw: address .../r/<role> and in every BW-ORG role declaration, so every declared role is addressable. Case-sensitive, lowercase [a-z0-9._-], 1-32 chars (umbrella Annex A).

Hash.description: Payload hash descriptor. hash_mode selects raw-byte hashing (the default) or the optional JSON-canonicalisation modes (jcs-sha256/jcs-sha512).

hash_mode.description: jcs-* modes apply RFC 8785 canonicalisation to a JSON payload before hashing; raw-* modes hash the raw payload bytes; manifest-* modes hash the deterministic-CBOR message manifest of a multipart payload (the I-D (Canonicalisation and Payload Hashing) Mode C).

RdpId.description: R7-04/R7-X1: the CANONICAL provider identifier, one value space. It was `{type: string, minLength: 1}` — so the grammar `rdpAuth` derives from a client certificate governed nothing downstream: every sample used `RDP:MockEU:001`, the reference path defaulted to `RDP:DEMO:OUT`, and `ds_accept_message(principal='not-a-canonical-rdp')` was accepted and stored as the ledger key. A precise identity rule over an unconstrained value space is a rule about nothing. Deployed legacy identifiers are NOT aliased: no alias policy is defined, because an alias that resolves to the same namespace is a second name for one thing, and two names is how R4-U3's collision returns.

KeyPackageRef.description: R9-03/R9-X1: the MLS reference to a KeyPackage, RFC 9420 §5.2 — `RefHash("MLS 1.0 KeyPackage Reference", KeyPackage)` over the ENCODED KeyPackage, using the hash function of the reservation's own cipher suite, encoded base64url WITHOUT padding. ONE definition, referenced everywhere the value appears: the reservation response that produces it, the invitation that quotes it, and the device credential bound to it. It was previously required by `InvitationDeposit` and produced by nothing — a value on the wire that no conforming client could construct, because neither the reservation request nor its response carried it and no document defined it. MLS already defines a reference for this object, so SBM does not define a second one.
KeyPackageRef.$comment: 43 characters is an unpadded base64url SHA-256; 86 an unpadded SHA-512. The suite decides which, so the bound is a range rather than a fixed length.

GroupInfoCommitment.description: R9-03 requirement 6: the commitment to the GroupInfo a Welcome delivers — `RefHash("SBM 1.0 GroupInfo Commitment", GroupInfo)` under the invitation's `offered_suite`, base64url without padding. Same construction as `KeyPackageRef` with its OWN label, so neither can be replayed as the other. Validated by the invited DEVICE after it decrypts the Welcome; the Delivery Service retains and echoes it and cannot parse what it commits to, which is why the earlier `{type: string}` claimed a binding no component could check.

IsoTimestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in Zulu (UTC, trailing Z) form (X-35). The Zulu form is normative: instant comparison (trust-store windows, as-of resolution, expiry ordering) is byte-wise on Zulu strings, which sort chronologically. format is asserted (FormatChecker) wherever schemas are validated.

MlsGroupId.description: MLS group identifier (RFC 9420), base64url-encoded (X-35: the base64url alphabet is schema-enforced; RFC 9420 leaves the length opaque).

MlsEpoch.description: MLS epoch at the time of the evidence event, as a DECIMAL STRING (no leading zeros). MLS defines the epoch as uint64 (RFC 9420), whose range exceeds the JSON safe-integer bound (2^53-1); a decimal string carries the full range exactly (M1/J0+; the I-D (Canonicalisation and Payload Hashing)).

AuthMethod.description: Sender-side authentication method bound to the SE-v1 submission, mapped to Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 CIR 2025/1944 REQ-QERDS-5.2.2-03. The mls-x509 / mls-uid-qeaa values are the profile default: authentication is performed inside the MLS handshake using the leaf-node QSealC or UID QEAA credential, corresponding to REQ-QERDS-5.2.2-03(c) (mutual TLS with an NCP certificate) or (d) (a digital signature under an NCP certificate). The +oidc4vp variants indicate an additional OpenID4VP ceremony at session setup for wallet-level policy enforcement (OPTIONAL). The remaining values record an alternative sender-authentication binding: two-factor = 5.2.2-03(a); wallet-eid-high / wallet-eid-substantial = 5.2.2-03(b) (European Digital Identity Wallet or notified eID at assurance level high/substantial); mtls-ncp = 5.2.2-03(c); ncp-signature = 5.2.2-03(d); cab-confirmed = 5.2.2-03(e).

RecipientAuthMethod.description: Recipient-side authentication method bound to DE-v1 issuance, mapped to Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 CIR 2025/1944 REQ-QERDS-5.2.2-03A. The means (or their combination) MUST ensure a very high level of confidence in the recipient's identity, and recipient identification MUST precede content delivery (Article 44(1)(c)). mfa = 5.2.2-03A(a); wallet-eid-high / wallet-eid-substantial = 5.2.2-03A(b); qes-qseal-cert = 5.2.2-03A(c) (certificate of a qualified electronic signature or seal); cab-confirmed = 5.2.2-03A(d).

EvidenceId.description: Unique identifier of this evidence object (ETSI EN 319 522-2 clause 8 component G01), distinct from message_id. RECOMMENDED: a UUIDv7, ULID, or URN.

PolicyId.description: Identifier (URI or OID URN) of the RDP evidence-issuance policy under which this evidence is produced (ETSI EN 319 522-2 clause 8 component R01).

Profile.description: Conformance profile under which this evidence is issued (spec §9.3, §13.3). 'production' is a CLAIM of QERDS-qualified status and the Regulation (EU) No 910/2014, Article 43(2) presumption — verifiable only in conjunction with the Trusted-List status of rdp_id, federation membership, the certificate chain, policy_id, and qualified-timestamp validation; a verifier MUST NOT treat this string alone as qualification. 'pilot' is non-qualified transitional evidence.

S3Attestation.description: Recipient digest-confirmation object for state S3 (the I-D (Message Flows and Delivery States), the I-D (Canonicalisation and Payload Hashing)): an authorised member/device decrypted the content and re-verified payload_hash within an authenticated recipient session (the TS clause 6), and signed or session-authenticated the FULL confirmation object bound to (message_id, mls_group_id, mls_epoch, acceptance_policy_ref, payload_hash, result, verified_at) — the wallet_signature_b64, when present, is a COSE_Sign1 whose payload is the deterministic-CBOR encoding of the object with the signature field removed (the I-D (Canonicalisation and Payload Hashing)), not a field subset. A precondition of DE-v1; result is always 'match' (a mismatch produces NDE-v1 payload-hash-mismatch with a recipient_confirmation instead). At least one proof — wallet_signature_b64 or session_authenticated — is REQUIRED.

allOf.$comment: R3 (twenty-fourth review): the SIGNED variant MUST identify the confirming device, so the COSE signer resolves to exactly that device's published confirmation_key (BW-MEMBER, TS INTF-1a/D) and its active-at-verified_at status is checkable. Without device_id the RDP can only confirm the MID has SOME ack-capable device — a retired or compromised one could sign.

wallet_signature_b64.description: Recipient wallet advanced electronic signature: a COSE_Sign1 whose payload is the deterministic-CBOR encoding of the confirmation object with wallet_signature_b64 removed (the same signed-payload construction as the RDP seal, the I-D (Evidence Objects and COSE Packaging)/the I-D (Canonicalisation and Payload Hashing)) — not over a chosen field subset. Base64 of the COSE_Sign1; the protected-header alg MUST be EdDSA(-8)/ES256(-7)/ES384(-35) (LINT-PKG-05). Present as an alternative to session_authenticated.

session_authenticated.description: The confirmation is bound to the authenticated recipient session of the TS clause 6 rather than to a standalone signature.

RecipientConfirmation.description: Recipient confirmation carried on NDE-v1 with reason payload-hash-mismatch (the I-D (Canonicalisation and Payload Hashing), R11): the recipient re-verified payload_hash after decryption and it did NOT match. At least one proof — wallet_signature_b64 or session_authenticated — is REQUIRED.

allOf.$comment: R3 (twenty-fourth review): the SIGNED variant MUST identify the confirming device, so the COSE signer resolves to exactly that device's published confirmation_key (BW-MEMBER, TS INTF-1a/D) and its active-at-verified_at status is checkable. Without device_id the RDP can only confirm the MID has SOME ack-capable device — a retired or compromised one could sign.

wallet_signature_b64.description: Recipient wallet advanced electronic signature: a COSE_Sign1 whose payload is the deterministic-CBOR encoding of the confirmation object with wallet_signature_b64 removed (the same signed-payload construction as the RDP seal, the I-D (Evidence Objects and COSE Packaging)/the I-D (Canonicalisation and Payload Hashing)) — not over a chosen field subset. Base64 of the COSE_Sign1; the protected-header alg MUST be EdDSA(-8)/ES256(-7)/ES384(-35) (LINT-PKG-05). Present as an alternative to session_authenticated.

AuthContext.description: Records which of the three identities (the TS clause 6 (identity proofing)) was authenticated for this evidence, by what method, at what assurance level, under whose authority. On SE-v1 it describes the sender side (method = auth_method); on DE-v1 the recipient side (method = recipient_auth_method).

identity.description: Which identity was authenticated: the legal entity (UID), a human member (MID/role), a system member / agent acting under a mandate (MID/role; member_type=system, Annex R), or the device/wallet instance (MLS leaf). identity=system records that an agent, not a person, was the acting identity (A1).

mid.description: The acting member's MID (pseudonymous), recorded when identity is member or system so the accountability chain resolves the acting member (Annex R, A1/A5). REQUIRED where identity=system (the acting agent must be identifiable); the MID resolves to a BW-MEMBER whose member_type matches the identity (bundle_lint LINT-BND-14).

method.description: The authentication method; equals the sibling auth_method (SE) or recipient_auth_method (DE).

authority.description: Reference to the QTSP/issuer or the organisation authorisation authority under whose authority the identity was established.

allOf.$comment: A1 (Annex R): a system acting identity must name the acting agent's MID.

Mandate.description: A system member's STANDING mandate — its scoped delegated authority (Annex R, A2). Reference-only: the mandate credential itself (an EAA / verifiable credential) travels end-to-end encrypted; only this reference is published in the signed BW-MEMBER so a counterparty can check the agent's authority before treating its messages as binding.

issuer.description: Issuer of the mandate attestation (a QTSP / the delegating entity's authority).

id.description: Stable identifier of the mandate attestation.

scope.description: The content classes the agent is authorised to act on (two-tier registry, §8.3a).

MandateRef.description: Reference on SE-v1 to the mandate an agent acted under for THIS message (Annex R, A2): issuer + id link to the system member's standing mandate (BW-MEMBER mandate_ref). REQUIRED on an SE whose auth_context.identity=system, forbidden otherwise (evidence_lint LINT-DE-14). The OPTIONAL mandate_commitment is a salted digest over (mandate id, scope, content_class) — salt confined to the E2EE envelope — so a verifier can confirm the acted-under scope covered the content class without the mandate or the class leaking (reveal procedure mirrors the grade commitment, TS clause 6).

opposable.description: Whether the agent's act is intended to be externally opposable (A1, nineteenth review). Default true (absent = opposable). When opposable, mandate_commitment is REQUIRED (evidence_lint LINT-DE-15) so a verifier can show the act was within the mandate's class scope without the mandate or class leaking. opposable=false marks a NON-opposable act: mandate_commitment is forbidden and mandate-scope conformance is then establishable only by internal audit, payload reveal, or the dispute path — never by external verification.

mandate_commitment.description: Salted SHA-256 commitment binding the acted-under mandate to the message's content class, anchored to the published BW-ORG version: SHA-256 of the deterministic-CBOR fixed-position array [dst=sm-mls:mandate-commitment:v2, salt, mandate_id, content_class, org_digest]. REQUIRED on an opposable system-member SE, FORBIDDEN where mandate_ref.opposable=false (LINT-DE-15). The 16-byte salt travels only in the E2EE envelope (mandate_commitment_salt); reveal mirrors the grade commitment (TS clause 6): recompute + check content_class is in the mandate's scope.

AcceptancePolicyRef.description: Reference to the BW-ORG-v1 acceptance policy IN FORCE at SE-v1 issuance (submission time), fixing BOTH the policy document (policy_version + doc_digest, stable across re-seals) AND the exact key selected within it (policy_key, F-08). A later policy change does not affect in-flight messages.

policy_key.description: F-08 (evidence 2.4): the EXACT acceptance_policy key selected for this message by the umbrella §8.3 deterministic selection (scoped -> the scope's acceptance_policy_ref key; default-scope role-addressed -> the role's key if present, else 'default'; entity-addressed -> 'default'). Makes every policy selection self-contained: two keys in the same BW-ORG can never produce indistinguishable evidence. Recomputed and enforced bundle-level (LINT-BND-30); signed by the sender (the X-03 tuple copies this ref).

ScopeRef.description: Reference to the confidentiality-scope descriptor (BW-ORG scope_map, spec §8.3a) in force at submission and applicable to the message. scope_id 'default' denotes the baseline (whole-pair) scope. Echoed in SE-v1 and DE-v1 for auditability (D6); the content_class that selected the scope is NOT carried in evidence.

Manifest.description: Ordered list of message parts for a multipart payload (the I-D (Canonicalisation and Payload Hashing) Mode C). The message-level payload_hash (hash_mode manifest-sha256/-sha512) is computed over the deterministic-CBOR manifest. Carries structure/metadata only — media types, lengths, per-part digests — never content. uniqueItems catches exact-duplicate entries; full part_id uniqueness and canonical byte-wise-ascending ordering are enforced by evidence_lint (LINT-MAN-01/02).

part_id.description: Unique, stable identifier of the part within the message. part_id values MUST be unique; the canonical manifest ordering is byte-wise ascending by part_id (the I-D (Canonicalisation and Payload Hashing)).

role.description: Role of the part in the message (closed registry, the I-D (Canonicalisation and Payload Hashing)).

length.description: Byte length of the part's decoded octets, as a DECIMAL STRING (no leading zeros) — a byte count has no natural safe-integer bound, so it is carried as a string for type-uniformity with mls_epoch (M1/J0+).

EnvelopeHash.description: R-02/D3 (evidence 2.2): the transmitted-octet commitment — SHA-256 (fixed by this type; no alg/mode selector, so SHA-512/JCS/manifest modes are unrepresentable) over the TLS-serialized RFC 9420 MLSMessage as handed to transport (the exact wire object, not the PrivateMessage alone; scripts/mls_wire.py is the reference serializer). `format` names the wire format/version. Independently recomputable by every party that handles the octets: RDP(out) at acceptance, every relaying RDP, RDP(in)/the wallet at receipt.

format.description: The committed wire object + version: RFC 9420 MLSMessage, protocol mls10, wire_format mls_private_message.

hex.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the serialized MLSMessage octets.

MlsStateHash.description: R-02/F-03/D3 (evidence 2.2): the MLS state commitment — SHA-256 (fixed by this type) over the TLS-serialized RFC 9420 §8.1 GroupContext. ONE value replacing the former enumerated {tree_hash, confirmed_transcript_hash} pair: the GroupContext contains protocol version, cipher_suite, group_id, epoch, tree_hash, confirmed_transcript_hash AND the extensions, so all are pinned together (two forks sharing group_id+epoch produce different commitments). Verification from evidence time: resolve the retained historical GroupContext, recompute this hash, then verify the retained ratchet tree against the GroupContext's tree_hash (the I-D, MLS state retention).

format.description: The committed struct + version: RFC 9420 §8.1 GroupContext, protocol mls10.

hex.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the serialized GroupContext octets.

SessionBinding.description: X-05 (evidence 2.3): a retained, privacy-aware binding of a session-authenticated confirmation to VERIFIABLE session material — a digest of the token / TLS exporter / session transcript, retained under the §4.3 duty for the evidence-retention period. Without it, a session confirmation is the provider-attested (narrowed) mode: a bare session_authenticated boolean cannot claim the member-grade proof mode (LINT-DE-20). TODO(legal): the narrowed claim's Article 43(2) weight for provider-attested confirmations awaits counsel.

digest.description: Lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the session material (never the material itself — privacy-aware).

RefusalConfirmation.description: X-29 (evidence 2.3): the RECIPIENT-PRODUCED proof of a member refusal — the s3-style choice: wallet-signed (device_id + wallet_signature_b64 over this object's own content minus the signature, the standard construction) or session-authenticated (with an optional SessionBinding; a bare boolean is the provider-attested narrowed mode). Covers the refused message and context so the refusal is independently attributable.

SenderConfirmation.description: X-03/D4 (evidence 2.3): the SENDER-WALLET-PRODUCED proof that the named sender authorised THESE bytes to THIS recipient — a wallet advanced electronic signature (the s3-signed construction: COSE_Sign1 over this object's deterministic CBOR with the signature field removed) under the sender member's published confirmation_key anchor, resolved per (mid, device_id) from the SENDER entity's BW-MEMBER (INTF-1b). The tuple includes the Batch-5 byte-exact commitments, so the sender independently signs the exact transmitted octets, and (R3-01) the sender and recipient ADDRESSES, so the sender signs the addressing decision that selects the acceptance policy. TODO(legal): the clause stating this signature's relation to the Article 44(1)(b) provider attestation (an additive second proof, never a substitute) and its Article 43(2) weight awaits counsel — D4 LEGAL-CONFIRM.

recipient_addr.description: R3-01/R3-T1: the address the message was sent TO. It was not a property of this tuple at all, so the addressing decision — which SELECTS the acceptance policy — sat outside the sender's signature and could be changed without invalidating it. Dropping it from a role-addressed submission silently selected the weaker 'default' policy. It is signed here now, and REQUIRED.

sender_addr.description: R3-01: the acting address the message was sent FROM, signed for the same reason — a confirmation that does not say who acted, in which role, leaves the acting identity outside the proof.

RecipientRevealConfirmation.description: DR-03 / R2-M1 (evidence 2.7): the RECIPIENT-PRODUCED proof accompanying a grade-commitment dispute. The recipient device's wallet advanced electronic signature (the s3-signed construction: COSE_Sign1 over this object's deterministic CBOR with the signature field removed) over the full dispute tuple, resolved against that device's published confirmation_key AS IT STOOD AT read_at (the as-of read; INTF-1/1a/2). HONEST SCOPE: this proves an ATTRIBUTABLE RECIPIENT ASSERTION — a named device of a named member asserted these values and is accountable for them. It does NOT prove the values were extracted from the disputed ciphertext; objective ciphertext-to-reveal proof would need a construction this profile does not define (recorded as specified future work). Before this existed, commitment INEQUALITY ALONE was treated as a valid rebuttal — and inequality is manufacturable by inventing a salt, so any provider could rebut any availability delivery.
